Setup now registers `context.onDispose` to stop the whole runtime, and Needs-you notifications are sent only while the plugin is active. For a disable no hook has seen yet, `NextSession.isCurrent` also checks `active()`, so a late planner answer neither pushes nor labels, and `Refresher.refresh` reads nothing while the plugin is disabled; the hub engine keeps running on purpose so re-enabling needs no rebuild.

Fixed in `1544b995b`. After the parallel manifest and git read, `serveTurn` now calls `turnEnv(turn)` again, so the `github` evidence, `state.env` and the planner's facts all use the branch the turn ended on. The manifest still probes on the earlier env, which is safe because the only git state it reads is whether a repository is there and its remotes, never which branch. `next.test.ts` covers a turn that switches branches.

Fixed in b33dc598d: the bind cleanup now bumps the bind generation before it detaches, so a `plugin_ui_get` still pending when the pane unmounts never attaches the chat it left. A one-key Send that was already made still reaches that chat.

Fixed in f83618bd27. `begin()` now only stages the new epoch. `activate()` promotes it once the replacement session is resident. Until then the resident session keeps its slot state, viewers and UI chain, and keeps serving invokes. A start that fails releases only its staged epoch, so a failed reopen leaves the working chat's suggestions as they were. `clearPlugin` also takes the epoch now, so a plugin that fails while the replacement is starting can't clear the resident copy.

Covered by "serves the resident session while a same-id start is pending and after it fails" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, plus the staging cases in `store.test.ts` and `service.teardown.test.ts`.

Valid, and it contradicts the comment a few lines above ("Once spawned, keep the shared startup lock until discovery is published. Cancelling a waiter must not let another waiter launch a duplicate daemon"). At `815be409c` the post-spawn probes had no signal; now both `probeHubForStartup` calls in the loop receive `signal`, so an abort throws an `AbortError` that the `catch` does not swallow, and the lock is released while the daemon is still booting. Impact is bounded by the OS-level `HubInstanceLock` (a duplicate daemon loses the singleton race), so low severity, but the fix is just dropping `signal` from those two calls; `deadline` already bounds them.

+	private async refreshList(force = false): Promise<void> {

+		// fetching would attribute old-account rows to the new scope. History
+		// omits cloud rows during the transition; reset refreshes them afterwards.

+			return

+			return this.listPromise

+			try {
+				void this.recoverAbandonedStarts()

+					return
+				}

+				for (const record of records) {
+					seen.add(record.id)
+					this.upsertRecord(record)
+				}

+				// example from the dashboard). Close its connection rather than keep
+				// it in History; the task on screen keeps its host so that opening it
+				// can explain the deletion (see explainConnectFailure).

+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+					void entry.host?.dispose("deleted").catch(() => undefined)
+				}

+			} catch (error) {

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) return

+					// the retained connections that nothing is using. The displayed task
+					// keeps its entry and host: closing them would leave a task on screen
+					// that cannot continue even after the user signs in again, and its
+					// next interaction reports the authentication failure itself.
+					for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {

+					}

+			} finally {
+				if (this.listPromise === listPromise) {

+				}
+			}
+		})()

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.
+			if (existing.agentStatus && isSettled(existing.agentStatus)) {
+				existing.agentStatus = this.rememberedStatusOf(record)
+			}
+			return existing
+		}

+			record,
+			pinned: 0,
+			agentStatus: this.rememberedStatusOf(record),

+	/** Changes account scope as one boundary: invalidate, detach, dispose, mutate scope, then reopen reads. */
+	async reset(changeScope?: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {

+			await previousTransition

+				await this.options.clearTask()
+			}

+			const hosts = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.host ? [entry.host] : []))
+			const connections = entries.flatMap((entry) => (entry.connection ? [entry.connection] : []))

+			// account active through every await, including DELETE; never retain old tokens.
+			void this.trackScopeOperation(() =>
+				Promise.allSettled([...connections, ...hosts.map((host) => host.dispose("accountScopeChanged"))]),
+			)

+			await changeScope?.()
+		})()

+		try {
+			await transition
+		} finally {
+			if (this.scopeTransition === transition) {
+				this.scopeTransition = undefined

+				// before a later auth/config refresh failed.
+				if (!this.disposed) {
+					this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()
+					void this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
+		// Enroll before executing any code that can yield or re-enter reset.
+		const promise = Promise.resolve().then(operation)
+		this.scopeOperations.add(promise)
+		return promise.finally(() => this.scopeOperations.delete(promise))
+	}

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {
+		let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+		try {
+			await Promise.race([
+				Promise.allSettled(operations),
+				new Promise<never>((_resolve, reject) => {
+					timer = setTimeout(
+						() =>
+							reject(
+								new Error(
+									"Cloud session cleanup is still pending. Your account has not changed; try again after cleanup finishes.",
+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])
+		} finally {
+			clearTimeout(timer)
+		}
+	}

+	private async connect(entry: CloudSessionEntry): Promise<CloudSessionHost> {
+		if (entry.connection) {

+		const sessionId = entry.record.id
+		const taskId = entry.record.metadata.taskId?.trim()
+		if (!taskId) {
+			throw new Error(`Cloud session ${sessionId} has no canonical task id.`)
+		}
+		const generation = this.scopeGeneration
+		const record = entry.record
+		const connection = (async () => {
+			const retainedHost = entry.host
+			const host =
+				retainedHost ??
+				(await CloudSessionHost.connect({
+					outerSessionId: sessionId,
+					taskId,
+					socketUrl: this.options.cloudSessions.sessionSocketUrl(sessionId),
+					getAuthToken: this.options.getAuthToken,
+					requestToolApproval: this.options.requestToolApproval,
+					telemetry: this.options.telemetry,
+					onStatusChange: (status) => {
+						// A replaced account entry must never receive its predecessor's events.
+						if (!this.disposed && generation === this.scopeGeneration && this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) {
+							this.handleStatusChange(sessionId, status)
+						}
+					},
+				}))
+			const status = retainedHost ? await retainedHost.refreshStatus() : host.status

+				await host.dispose("accountScopeChanged").catch(() => undefined)

+			}
+			entry.host = host
+			// A later list may invalidate the snapshot while the RPC is pending.
+			if (entry.record === record) {
+				entry.agentStatus = status
+				if (isSettled(status)) this.rememberStatus(record, status, Date.now())
+			}

+			return host
+		})()

+		try {
+			return await connection
+		} finally {
+			if (entry.connection === connection) entry.connection = undefined
+		}
+	}
+
+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+		if (!entry) {
+			return
+		}
+		const previous = entry.agentStatus
+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {
+			this.rememberStatus(entry.record, status, now)
+		}
+		// Learning the current status on connect is not agent activity; only a
+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.
+		if (previous !== undefined && previous !== status) {
+			entry.lastActivityAt = now
+		}
+		this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()

+		if (!isDisplayed && previous !== undefined && previous !== status && (status === "completed" || status === "failed")) {
+			this.notifyFinished(entry, status)
+		}
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+	}
+
+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const title = entry.title ?? entry.record.title?.trim() ?? entry.record.repoContext.repoUrl ?? entry.record.id

+			.showMessage({
+				type: status === "failed" ? ShowMessageType.WARNING : ShowMessageType.INFORMATION,
+				message: `${label}: ${title}`,

+	private ensurePolling(): void {

+	/**

+	/** Resolves live status only for cloud rows a caller is about to display. */

+			for (let sessionId = pendingIds.shift(); sessionId; sessionId = pendingIds.shift()) {
+				const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+				if (!entry || this.statusOf(entry) !== "unknown") continue
+				try {
+					if (entry.connection) {
+						await entry.connection
+						changed = true
+						continue
+					}

+					if (lastAttempt !== undefined && now - lastAttempt < STATUS_RESOLUTION_RETRY_MS) continue

+			}
+		}

+			Array.from({ length: Math.min(STATUS_RESOLUTION_CONCURRENCY, pendingIds.length) }, () => resolveNext()),
+		)

+	private async refreshList(force = false): Promise<void> {

+		// fetching would attribute old-account rows to the new scope. History
+		// omits cloud rows during the transition; reset refreshes them afterwards.
+		if (this.scopeTransition || this.disposed) return

+			return
+		}

+			return this.listPromise
+		}

+		let listPromise!: Promise<void>
+		listPromise = (async () => {
+			try {
+				void this.recoverAbandonedStarts()

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) {
+					return
+				}
+				const seen = new Set<string>()
+				for (const record of records) {
+					seen.add(record.id)
+					this.upsertRecord(record)
+				}
+				// A record that left the account's list was deleted elsewhere (for
+				// example from the dashboard). Close its connection rather than keep
+				// it in History; the task on screen keeps its host so that opening it
+				// can explain the deletion (see explainConnectFailure).
+				for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+					if (seen.has(id) || this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue
+					this.entries.delete(id)
+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+					void entry.host?.dispose("deleted").catch(() => undefined)
+				}
+				this.pruneRememberedStatuses(seen)
+				this.listFetchedAt = Date.now()
+			} catch (error) {
+				// Reset invalidates both successful responses and failed requests.
+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) return
+				if (error instanceof CloudSessionError && error.code === "authentication_required") {

+					// the retained connections that nothing is using. The displayed task
+					// keeps its entry and host: closing them would leave a task on screen
+					// that cannot continue even after the user signs in again, and its
+					// next interaction reports the authentication failure itself.
+					for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+						if (this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue

+						this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)

+					}
+				}
+				// Keep the last snapshot; History still renders local tasks.
+				Logger.warn("[CloudSessions] Failed to refresh cloud session list:", error)
+				this.listFetchedAt = Date.now()
+			} finally {
+				if (this.listPromise === listPromise) {
+					this.listPromise = undefined
+				}
+			}
+		})()

+		return listPromise
+	}

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {
+		const existing = this.entries.get(record.id)

+			existing.record = record

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.
+			if (existing.agentStatus && isSettled(existing.agentStatus)) {
+				existing.agentStatus = this.rememberedStatusOf(record)
+			}
+			return existing
+		}

+			record,
+			pinned: 0,
+			agentStatus: this.rememberedStatusOf(record),
+			lastActivityAt: Date.parse(record.updatedAt) || Date.now(),

+		return entry
+	}

+	/** Changes account scope as one boundary: invalidate, detach, dispose, mutate scope, then reopen reads. */
+	async reset(changeScope?: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {

+			if (this.scopeTransition === transition) {

+				// before a later auth/config refresh failed.

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
+		// Enroll before executing any code that can yield or re-enter reset.
+		const promise = Promise.resolve().then(operation)

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {

+			await Promise.race([

+				new Promise<never>((_resolve, reject) => {
+					timer = setTimeout(
+						() =>
+							reject(
+								new Error(
+									"Cloud session cleanup is still pending. Your account has not changed; try again after cleanup finishes.",
+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])
+		} finally {
+			clearTimeout(timer)
+		}
+	}

+	private async connect(entry: CloudSessionEntry): Promise<CloudSessionHost> {
+		if (entry.connection) {

+		const taskId = entry.record.metadata.taskId?.trim()

+		}

+		const record = entry.record
+		const connection = (async () => {
+			const retainedHost = entry.host
+			const host =
+				retainedHost ??
+				(await CloudSessionHost.connect({
+					outerSessionId: sessionId,
+					taskId,
+					socketUrl: this.options.cloudSessions.sessionSocketUrl(sessionId),
+					getAuthToken: this.options.getAuthToken,
+					requestToolApproval: this.options.requestToolApproval,
+					telemetry: this.options.telemetry,
+					onStatusChange: (status) => {
+						// A replaced account entry must never receive its predecessor's events.
+						if (!this.disposed && generation === this.scopeGeneration && this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) {
+							this.handleStatusChange(sessionId, status)
+						}
+					},
+				}))
+			const status = retainedHost ? await retainedHost.refreshStatus() : host.status
+			if (this.disposed || generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.entries.get(sessionId) !== entry) {
+				await host.dispose("accountScopeChanged").catch(() => undefined)

+			}
+			entry.host = host
+			// A later list may invalidate the snapshot while the RPC is pending.
+			if (entry.record === record) {
+				entry.agentStatus = status
+				if (isSettled(status)) this.rememberStatus(record, status, Date.now())
+			}

+			return host
+		})()

+		try {
+			return await connection
+		} finally {
+			if (entry.connection === connection) entry.connection = undefined
+		}
+	}
+
+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+		if (!entry) {
+			return
+		}
+		const previous = entry.agentStatus
+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {
+			this.rememberStatus(entry.record, status, now)
+		}
+		// Learning the current status on connect is not agent activity; only a
+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.
+		if (previous !== undefined && previous !== status) {
+			entry.lastActivityAt = now
+		}
+		this.options.invalidateHistoryCache()

+		if (!isDisplayed && previous !== undefined && previous !== status && (status === "completed" || status === "failed")) {
+			this.notifyFinished(entry, status)
+		}
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+	}
+
+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	private ensurePolling(): void {

discussion_comments.comment_body: Not fixing this here. This read-then-attach order dates back to the original cloud runtime commit; it isn't new in this PR. The window is a single `readMessages` round trip, and if the reply lands in it, reopening the task re-reads the transcript and shows it. Buffering events across the read adds a lot of reconciliation code for a narrow, self-healing case.

Valid, fixed in a65115d1c. The pending-start entry in sessionStarts now records an abort issued while the start is in flight; a turn that waited on that start completes as aborted (done event, aborted result) without running on the replacement. The agent runtime ignores an abort before run() starts, so this has to be decided at the host before the turn is dispatched. Regression test: B sends during A's rebuild, aborts before it finishes, the turn resolves aborted with neither agent's run called, and the replacement takes the next turn normally.

Good catch, fixed in efd698c2e. The replacement is now built first and takes over the map entry (the same shape as pre-#14501), and the old runtime object is released afterwards with a guard so it cannot evict the newcomer. There is no longer a window without a resident session, and a failed rebuild leaves the idle resident untouched (test added).

Agreed, fixed in 7dd54f630. The release is now gated on the resident no longer occupying its slot (this.sessions.get(sessionId) !== resident). That gives the right outcome in all three cases: success (live replacement holds the slot, old runtime released), a rebuild that registered and then failed (its cleanup empties the slot, old runtime released, nothing stranded), and a rebuild that threw before registering (resident still holds the slot, left untouched and reachable). Test flipped back to assert the resident survives an early build failure.

`request()` coalesces a newer request into `pending`, but it doesn't invalidate an already-active rebuild for the same reason — `cancellationGeneration` only moves in `cancel()` (line 40). So the active run's `isCurrent()` stays `true`, and once it finishes the newer request rebuilds the session again.

There's a correctness window here, not just redundant work. If the active rebuild has already snapshotted its config when the newer setting arrives, it installs the superseded one; and for checkpoint rebuilds it can replay a deferred follow-up from the shared `checkpointTransition` before the newer rebuild applies the latest setting — so a real message can run under the old checkpoint config.

I don't think bumping the generation here is a self-contained fix: the transition object is shared between the active and queued requests, and an invalidated rebuild returning from `replaceActiveSession()` can still clear `this.checkpointTransition` and stop the replacement. Either make a same-reason request explicitly supersede the active run with the transition ownership handled to match, or rename `isCurrent()` so it's clear it only means "not cancelled". A scheduler test for requesting a reason while that reason is actively rebuilding would pin whichever contract you pick.

Thanks — you were right on both counts, and the second one hid a real defect.

`isCurrent()` in a78223a means exactly "no newer request for the same reason has arrived": `request()` stamps a per-reason generation, and a running rebuild's context reads it live. `cancel()` and the per-reason cancellation generation are gone; nothing could reach them because `runTaskTransition` waits for the drain first.

The shared `checkpointTransition` is gone too. Holding a follow-up outside Core's queue meant nothing rendered it: a message typed during a turn after toggling Checkpoints vanished from the chat until the turn ended (this is what the e2e was failing on across all three CI platforms). Follow-ups now always go to Core's queue. The scheduler treats a session with queued prompts as busy, since Core drains the queue the instant a turn ends, and a send that settles after Core already started the next queued turn no longer flips the session idle. There is a scheduler test for a same-reason request during an active rebuild, and coordinator tests for supersession before replacement.
